newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - April regrade trades at +30cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - April regrade trades at +30cts.

text.p: Singapore swaps jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) traded late afteroon on Thursday at positive levels despite the large negative spread on the physical market, traders said.
"The regrade is still positive in the swaps market because the physical gas oil is being artificially held up," one trader said.
April regrade was last quoted at 15/30 cents against offers at 20 cents on Wednesday. Earlier in the day April traded at 25-30 cents, brokers said.
In the physical market, gas oil is currently priced on average at about 90 cents per barrel above jet fuel for prompt cargoes, the source said.
This is primarily due to the large purchases of more than three million barrels of gas oil by a Singapore trader since the start of this month, traders said.
"It is too early to say if the regrade would turn negative in the second quarter as there are still committments to be covered," said another refining source.
He said that surplus physical jet fuel should be entering the market sometime in mid-April.
The April gas oil was last quoted at $26.20/$26.40, down from Wednesday's $26.60/$26.70, but unchanged from the morning in quiet trade, brokers said.
Sources said the lower level were a correction to the steep hike to swap prices late yesterday. But most expected prices to remain high as the Singapore trader's buying spree has yet to end.
The fuel oil swaps market were steady but were expected to pick up slightly later in the day on expectations of buying from a local trader.
April fuel oil swaps were last quoted $102.00/$103.00 per tonne, down from Wednesday's $103.00/104.00 per tonne, brokers said.
They said April swaps traded earlier in the day at $102.00 per tonne compared to the $103.00 traded high late Tuesday.
The latest run up was primarily due to the emergence of a local trader to buy prompt cargoes on the Singapore physical market which expected to last for a few days at least.
On Wednesday, the trader was bidding for two 20,000-tonne cargoes at $103.00 per tonne free-on-board basis, up $2.00 from Tuesday's buying level.
